key: When the people do not fear what they ought to fear, that which is their great dread will come on them.
s: Opening a chapter on the people and the sage, the verse gives a warning; Wang Bi, on chapter 72, takes it to mean that once stillness and humility give way to reliance on might, might no longer holds the people, and Heaven’s punishment comes.
src: Wang Bi, Laozi zhu, chapter 72, zh.wikisource (the Huating Zhang edition), revision 2354026 (2024)

opened.edition: zh.wikisource 道德經 (王弼本), the 華亭張氏 edition, revision 2354026
opened.locator: chapter 72, comment on 民不畏威，則大威至。無狎其所居，無厭其所生。

evidence.words: 離其清淨，行其躁欲，棄其謙後，任其威權，則物擾而民僻，威不能復制民，民不能堪其威，則上下大潰矣，天誅將至。故曰，民不畏威，則大威至。
evidence.gloss: If one departs from clear stillness, follows restless desire, casts off humility and keeping behind, and relies on awesome power, things are disturbed and the people go astray; might can no longer control the people, the people cannot bear the might, high and low collapse, and Heaven’s punishment is about to come. Hence it says: when the people do not fear might, great might arrives.

reason: Problem holds: ‘warning’ stood on both sides of the semicolon. Only the second is dropped (‘takes it to mean that’); the reading is unchanged and still rests on Wang Bi’s comment in packet.js tao 72 (revision 2354026), 離其清淨…天誅將至。故曰，民不畏威，則大威至, re-opened and found verbatim. verse.js ok (at [71]); entry-check ok (44 words).
